Chef, I will bring everything quickly now.
Nastya, stop, I urgently need help!
What happened, Max? What is it?
Tell the guest that the truffles are bad today.
Let him order any other dish!
No, I cannot say that.
The guest came especially for this salad.
But I do not have this truffle!
He is a very strict and important person.
By the way, he asked to give you a note.
Oh no, this is a disaster for the kitchen!
Hurry, the chef is already getting very angry.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'trouble, misfortune' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('in trouble') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну, допустим, я жулик. А ты жадина и не помогаешь людям в беде.
examples.trans: All right, let's say I'm a crook. But you're greedy, and you don't help people in trouble.

meanings.note: a particular prepared food item or meal course

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Secondary conversational sense ('different') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'note' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Кстати, он просил передать тебе записку.
examples.trans: By the way, he asked to give you a note.

examples.text: Она не успела оставить тебе записку!
examples.trans: It did not have time to leave you a note!

злиться.gloss: to be angry, to get mad

meanings.en: to be angry, to get mad
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be angry', forming an aspectual pair with 'разозлиться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: А знаешь, почему ты так злишься?
examples.trans: And do you know why you are so angry?
Don't be angry with me, please.

examples.text: Хорошо. А знаешь, почему ты так злишься?
examples.trans: Fine. Do you know why you're so angry?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'catastrophe, disaster' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for us!

examples.text: Это просто катастрофа для нашей кампании!
examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for our campaign!

examples.text: О нет, это катастрофа для кухни!
examples.trans: Oh no, this is a disaster for the kitchen!

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'by the way'.
Secondary conversational sense ('handy, well-timed') (это очень кстати) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'any', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Любая обезьяна эти выборы выиграет! Ты что, хуже обезьяны?
examples.trans: Any monkey will win this election! What, are you worse than a monkey?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: playful derogatory nickname used by Chef Barinov for Max

examples.trans: Runt, are you still standing here?
The chef often called the newcomer a runt.

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Secondary conversational sense ('alone') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over, to give
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pass on', forming an aspectual pair with 'передавать'.

examples.trans: Please pass on my regards to your mum.

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.

Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to understand', forming an aspectual pair with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Ты точно понял, как нужно правильно нарезать этот стейк?
examples.trans: Did you definitely understand how to slice this steak properly?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пасть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to hit', forming an aspectual pair with 'попадать'.

meanings.en: to get to, to end up
meanings.note: как попасть в центр? = how do I get to the centre?

examples.trans: A firework hit the power station.
How do I get to the station?

examples.text: Скажи: салют попал в станцию. Три района без света.
examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come', forming an aspectual pair with 'приходить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Secondary conversational sense ('to beg') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for the sake of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: Work, work. It's all for us.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'алат'). Common masculine noun meaning 'salad' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.

examples.text: Гость пришёл специально ради этого салата.
examples.trans: The guest came especially for this salad.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'едьмой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('seventh').

examples.text: Седьмой столик заказал салат с трюфелями.
examples.trans: Table seven ordered a salad with truffles.
Look, the woman at the seventh table!

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'strongly'.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to happen', forming an aspectual pair with 'случаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: не специально = not on purpose, by accident
Secondary conversational sense ('specially, specifically') (for a particular purpose) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну перестаньте, вы же не специально!
examples.trans: Oh, stop it, you didn't do it on purpose!

examples.text: Я приготовил этот торт специально для вас.
examples.trans: I made this cake specially for you.
Are you doing this on purpose?

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'small table'.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Стоять на месте, никто не выходит из кухни без разрешения!
examples.trans: Freeze right there, nobody leaves the kitchen without permission!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трогий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strict, stern').

examples.trans: How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

examples.text: У нас в школе очень строгий директор.
examples.trans: We have a very strict principal at our school.

examples.text: Ой, спина не разгибается! Какая вы строгая, Клавдия Викторовна.
examples.trans: Ow, my back won't straighten! How strict you are, Klavdia Viktorovna.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

тащить.gloss: to drag, to pull, to carry, to bring

meanings.note: colloquial: fetch or drag something

examples.trans: Then run, go grab a clothespin quickly!

examples.text: Тащи свою птицу су-шефу на стол!
examples.trans: Drag your bird to the sous-chef's table!

торопиться.gloss: to be in a hurry, to hurry

meanings.en: to be in a hurry, to rush
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be in a hurry', forming an aspectual pair with 'поторопиться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'truffle', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Шеф, дорогой, а трюфели тебе надо?
examples.trans: Chef, my dear, do you need truffles?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Secondary conversational sense ('people') (plural люди, a different word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
